text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD-22748 triggered for service inference-gateway: 5xx error rate > 3% in us-west1 (2m). Severity: high. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-22748

maya: ack'd. i'm on it — starting triage.

pagerduty: PD-22748 acknowledged by maya at 2026-03-14T02:12:11Z

alex: seeing a jump in 504s from the gateway to inference backends. graph: https://grafana/redwood/d/igw/5xx?orgId=1&var-region=us-west1

jordan: tailing runtime logs, looks like kv-cache eviction thrash + long GPU queue times. autoscaler didn't spin up new pods for the last surge.

maya: can we hot-fix routing to push traffic off the overloaded pool? if we can split to fallback model variant it should reduce latency and 5xxs.

jordan: agree. proposing temporary traffic split: 75% primary -> 25% fallback (fallback is quantized v1.3, compatible interface)

alex: confirmed pods in nodepool us-west1-a are at 100% and Pending queue growing. here's hpa/scale info:
```
kubectl get hpa -n inference
NAME            REFERENCE              TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
inference-hpa   Deployment/inference   120%/80%      3        30        30      4h
```

alex: HPA max hit. autoscaler logs show provisioning error -> quotaExceeded from cloud provider (we're out of burst capacity in that AZ).

maya: ok, plan: 1) flip routing to fallback variant 2) disable canary traffic we rolled out 10m ago 3) contact cloud-ops to request emergency burst quota 4) notify CS for impacted customers.

samira: i'll draft status page blurb and notify account leads for acme-corp and lexar.ai — both show elevated error rates in their telemetry.

jordan: to flip routing do this (admin API):
```
curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/v1/config/traffic-split \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"service":"inference-gateway","region":"us-west1","split":[{"model":"primary","weight":75},{"model":"fallback-v1.3","weight":25}]}'
```

maya: executing now. posting result.

maya: POST returned 200. traffic-split updated. routing change propagating (expected <30s).

incident-bot: Alert: service inference-gateway 5xx rate decreased to 1.1% (us-west1) — showing downward trend.

alex: dumping a handful of error traces: most are upstream timeout (504) and connection reset by peer. pushing hints to runtime team to add more aggressive retry/backoff on gateway side.

jordan: warming KV cache on fallback nodes to avoid cold-start penalty. run: `./tools/warm_kv.sh --region us-west1 --model fallback-v1.3`

support-bot: Notified customers: acme-corp, lexar.ai, tide-labs via account.slack.

samira: status page update posted: https://status.redwood/incidents/PD-22748 — note: partial degradation in us-west1, mitigation in progress.

maya: cloud-ops reply: can provision 4 nodes in us-west1-b but still verifying capacity in a. queued the emergency quota request.

lee: i'm the night oncall, ETA 30m. maya — any handoff notes?

maya: handoff in 30m. current state: routing split 75/25 to fallback, error rate dropped from 3.6% -> ~1.0%, some customer errors persist (~0.4% of global traffic). canary disabled. cloud-ops provisioning in progress. open follow-ups: confirm full drain of overloaded pods, revert split when queue depth normal.

alex: created follow-up runbook checklist in incident doc: https://docs.redwood/incidents/PD-22748-runbook

jordan: recommend postmortem action items: add cross-AZ burst quota alarms, adjust HPA target to avoid hard maxing, and add a warmup policy for fallback models.

samira: i'll coordinate customer comms and include timeline.

incident-bot: PD-22748 auto-close check in 60m if no regression.

maya: thanks all — i'll update once cloud nodes are provisioned or if error rate climbs. :pray:

lee: ack. i'll monitor and take over if anything moves after handoff. :eyes:
